name: Eunus
bio: A Syrian slave and reputed prophet who led the First Servile War in Sicily, where rebels held cities and proclaimed him king for several years.

name: Spartacus
bio: A Thracian gladiator who led the largest slave revolt against Rome. His army of escaped slaves defeated several Roman forces before being crushed in southern Italy.

name: Boudica
bio: Queen of the Iceni who led a revolt against Roman occupation of Britain after Roman officials seized her family’s lands and assaulted her and her daughters.

name: Mazdak
bio: A Persian reformer who preached that land and wealth should be shared in common. His movement won royal support before its followers were massacred.

name: John Ball
bio: A radical priest who preached that all people were created equal, and a leader of the English Peasants’ Revolt.

name: Wat Tyler
bio: Leader of the English Peasants’ Revolt, killed while negotiating with King Richard II at Smithfield.

name: Thomas Müntzer
bio: A radical preacher who joined the German Peasants’ War, teaching that the common people should overthrow their lords. He was executed after the defeat at Frankenhausen.

name: Bartolomé de las Casas
bio: A Spanish friar who gave up his own Indigenous laborers and spent fifty years denouncing the conquest’s cruelty, though he once proposed African slaves as a substitute and later repented of it.

name: Gerrard Winstanley
bio: Leader of the Diggers, who planted common land in 1649 and argued that the earth should be a common treasury for all.

name: Zumbi dos Palmares
bio: Leader of Palmares, a long-lived community of escaped slaves in northeastern Brazil. The day of his death is Brazil’s Black Consciousness Day.

name: Nanny of the Maroons
bio: A leader of the Windward Maroons in Jamaica who fought British forces from the mountains. She is a national hero of Jamaica.

name: Túpac Amaru II
bio: A descendant of Inca rulers who led a great Indigenous uprising in Peru against Spanish colonial exploitation. He was executed in Cusco.

name: Túpac Katari
bio: An Aymara leader who besieged La Paz for months during the Andean uprising of 1781. He was executed by the Spanish.

name: Toussaint Louverture
bio: A formerly enslaved man who became the leading general of the Haitian Revolution. Captured by Napoleon’s forces, he died in a French prison.

name: Jean-Jacques Dessalines
bio: Toussaint’s lieutenant who defeated Napoleon’s army and declared Haiti’s independence in 1804.

name: Olympe de Gouges
bio: A playwright who wrote the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen in 1791. She was guillotined during the Terror.

name: Mary Wollstonecraft
bio: Philosopher and author of A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, a founding text of feminism.

name: Gracchus Babeuf
bio: Leader of the Conspiracy of the Equals, which aimed to complete the French Revolution with common ownership. He was executed.

name: Thomas Paine
bio: Author of Common Sense and Rights of Man, who also proposed a basic endowment for every citizen funded by a tax on land.

name: Robert Owen
bio: A mill owner turned socialist who cut hours and built schools at New Lanark and helped found the cooperative movement.

name: Tecumseh
bio: A Shawnee leader who built a confederation of Native nations to resist the seizure of their lands by the United States.

name: Simón Bolívar
bio: The leader of independence wars that freed much of South America from Spanish rule.

name: Denmark Vesey
bio: A free Black carpenter in Charleston who was executed for planning a major slave uprising.

name: Nat Turner
bio: An enslaved preacher who led a rebellion in Virginia in 1831. He was hanged after weeks in hiding.

name: John Brown
bio: A white abolitionist who led a raid on the federal armory at Harpers Ferry to arm enslaved people. He was hanged for treason.

name: Flora Tristan
bio: A French-Peruvian writer who called for a universal workers’ union years before the Communist Manifesto and linked women’s emancipation to workers’ liberation.

name: Louis Auguste Blanqui
bio: A French revolutionary who spent about half of his life in prison for his insurrections.

name: Sojourner Truth
bio: She escaped slavery in New York and became a renowned abolitionist and women’s rights speaker.

name: Frederick Douglass
bio: He escaped slavery and became the most influential abolitionist orator and writer in America, and a champion of women’s suffrage.

name: Harriet Tubman
bio: She escaped slavery and returned again and again to guide others to freedom, then served as a Union scout and spy in the Civil War.

name: Karl Marx
bio: A philosopher and economist whose critique of capitalism in Capital remains the foundation of socialist thought.

name: Friedrich Engels
bio: Marx’s collaborator and the editor of Capital’s later volumes, who documented the conditions of Manchester’s working class.

name: Louise Michel
bio: A schoolteacher who fought on the barricades of the Paris Commune. Deported to New Caledonia, she sided with the Kanak uprising there.

name: Eugène Pottier
bio: A Paris Commune member who wrote the words of The Internationale in 1871.

name: Peter Kropotkin
bio: A Russian prince turned anarchist, whose book Mutual Aid argued that cooperation drives evolution as much as competition.

name: William Morris
bio: A designer, poet and socialist who wanted to restore beauty and joy to labor.

name: Eleanor Marx
bio: Marx’s youngest daughter and an organizer of the gasworkers’ and dockers’ unions in London.

name: Mother Jones
bio: Mary Harris Jones, an Irish-born organizer who led mine workers’ strikes and marched child mill workers to the president’s house.

name: Lucy Parsons
bio: A labor radical of Black, Mexican and Native ancestry who co-founded the IWW and campaigned for the Haymarket defendants, including her husband.

name: Eugene V. Debs
bio: A railway union leader who became a socialist and ran for president five times, once from prison, winning nearly a million votes.

name: Joe Hill
bio: A Swedish-born IWW songwriter executed in Utah on a murder conviction widely seen as a frame-up.

name: Frank Little
bio: An IWW organizer lynched in Butte, Montana, while supporting a strike of copper miners.

name: Emma Goldman
bio: An anarchist writer and speaker who campaigned for free speech, birth control and workers’ rights, and was deported from the US in 1919.

name: Rosa Luxemburg
bio: A Marxist economist and revolutionary who opposed the First World War and was murdered after the Spartacist uprising.

name: Karl Liebknecht
bio: The only member of the German parliament to vote against war credits in December 1914. He was murdered alongside Luxemburg.

name: Clara Zetkin
bio: A German socialist who led the international socialist women’s movement and proposed International Women’s Day.

name: Alexandra Kollontai
bio: A Bolshevik who championed women’s liberation and later became one of the world’s first women ambassadors.

name: Vladimir Lenin
bio: Leader of the Bolshevik Party and of the October Revolution of 1917.

name: Leon Trotsky
bio: A leader of the 1917 revolution and founder of the Red Army who became Stalin’s leading opponent. He was assassinated in Mexico.

name: Antonio Gramsci
bio: An Italian communist imprisoned by Mussolini, whose Prison Notebooks developed the theory of hegemony.

name: Emiliano Zapata
bio: A leader of the Mexican Revolution who fought for peasants’ land under the slogan “Land and liberty.”

name: Ricardo Flores Magón
bio: A Mexican anarchist journalist whose newspaper Regeneración helped prepare the Mexican Revolution. He died in a US prison.

name: James Connolly
bio: An Irish socialist and union leader who commanded rebel forces in the Easter Rising and was executed by a British firing squad.

name: Jim Larkin
bio: An Irish union leader who led Dublin’s workers through the 1913 Lockout.

name: Ida B. Wells
bio: A journalist who documented lynching in the American South and co-founded the NAACP.

name: W. E. B. Du Bois
bio: A sociologist and historian who co-founded the NAACP and wrote The Souls of Black Folk and Black Reconstruction.

name: Hubert Harrison
bio: A Harlem socialist street orator and writer, called the father of Harlem radicalism.

name: A. Philip Randolph
bio: He organized the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, the first major Black-led union, and conceived the 1963 March on Washington.

name: Claudia Jones
bio: A Trinidad-born communist and feminist deported from the US to Britain, where she founded the West Indian Gazette and helped start the Notting Hill Carnival.

name: Paul Robeson
bio: A singer, actor and athlete whose passport was revoked for his left-wing politics and anti-colonial activism.

name: C. L. R. James
bio: A Trinidadian historian and Marxist who wrote The Black Jacobins.

name: José Carlos Mariátegui
bio: A Peruvian Marxist who argued that Latin American socialism must start from Indigenous communal traditions.

name: Augusto César Sandino
bio: A Nicaraguan general who led a guerrilla war against US Marine occupation. He was assassinated on the orders of Anastasio Somoza.

name: Farabundo Martí
bio: A Salvadoran communist executed after the 1932 uprising. The guerrilla front of the 1980s took his name.

name: Ho Chi Minh
bio: Leader of Vietnam’s independence movement against French and then American power.

name: Bhagat Singh
bio: An Indian socialist revolutionary hanged by the British at 23. His slogan was “Long live revolution.”

name: B. R. Ambedkar
bio: A Dalit jurist, economist and campaigner against caste who led the drafting of India’s constitution.

name: Mohandas Gandhi
bio: Leader of mass nonviolent resistance to British rule in India.

name: Sylvia Pankhurst
bio: A suffragette who broke with her family to organize working-class women in London’s East End, later championing Ethiopian independence.

name: Dolores Ibárruri
bio: A Spanish communist known as La Pasionaria, whose cry “They shall not pass” became the slogan of the defense of Madrid.

name: Buenaventura Durruti
bio: A Spanish anarchist who led a militia column in the Civil War and died defending Madrid.

name: Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti
bio: Italian immigrant anarchists executed in Massachusetts after a trial condemned worldwide as unjust.

name: Emma Tenayuca
bio: A Mexican-American organizer who led the 1938 strike of pecan shellers in San Antonio at age 21.

name: Kwame Nkrumah
bio: Leader of Ghana’s independence and a leading voice of pan-Africanism.

name: Patrice Lumumba
bio: The first elected prime minister of the independent Congo, overthrown and executed within months of taking office.

name: Amílcar Cabral
bio: Leader of the liberation struggle in Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde, assassinated shortly before independence.

name: Frantz Fanon
bio: A Martinican psychiatrist who joined the Algerian revolution and wrote The Wretched of the Earth.

name: Aimé Césaire
bio: A Martinican poet and politician, co-founder of the Négritude movement and author of Discourse on Colonialism.

name: Agostinho Neto
bio: A poet and doctor who led Angola’s liberation movement and became its first president.

name: Samora Machel
bio: Leader of Mozambique’s liberation struggle and its first president, killed in a plane crash.

name: Thomas Sankara
bio: Burkina Faso’s revolutionary president, who pushed land reform, mass vaccination and women’s rights before he was assassinated.

name: Walter Rodney
bio: A Guyanese historian who wrote How Europe Underdeveloped Africa. He was killed by a bomb in Georgetown.

name: Steve Biko
bio: Founder of South Africa’s Black Consciousness Movement. He died from injuries sustained in police custody.

name: Ruth First
bio: A South African communist journalist and scholar killed by a parcel bomb sent by apartheid agents.

name: Chris Hani
bio: Leader of the South African Communist Party, assassinated a year before South Africa’s first democratic election.

name: Nelson Mandela
bio: A leader of the anti-apartheid struggle who spent 27 years in prison and became South Africa’s first democratically elected president.

name: Che Guevara
bio: An Argentine doctor who became a commander of the Cuban Revolution. He was executed in Bolivia.

name: Fidel Castro
bio: Leader of the Cuban Revolution and of Cuba for nearly fifty years.

name: Salvador Allende
bio: A Marxist doctor elected president of Chile in 1970. He died during the military coup.

name: Víctor Jara
bio: A Chilean singer of the New Song movement, tortured and killed in the days after the coup.

name: Rosa Parks
bio: A seasoned NAACP activist whose arrest for refusing to give up her bus seat launched the Montgomery boycott.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
bio: A leader of the civil rights movement who was organizing a Poor People’s Campaign and supporting Memphis sanitation strikers when he was assassinated.

name: Malcolm X
bio: A minister and revolutionary who became a powerful voice for Black self-determination and internationalism.

name: Ella Baker
bio: A civil rights organizer who mentored the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee and championed grassroots, group-centered leadership.

name: Fannie Lou Hamer
bio: A Mississippi sharecropper who became a voting rights leader and co-founded the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party.

name: Bayard Rustin
bio: A gay socialist pacifist who was the chief organizer of the 1963 March on Washington.

name: Fred Hampton
bio: Chairman of the Illinois Black Panther Party, killed at 21 in a police raid organized with the FBI.

name: Cesar Chavez
bio: Co-founder of the United Farm Workers, who led the Delano grape boycott.

name: Dolores Huerta
bio: Co-founder of the United Farm Workers, a negotiator and organizer who coined the slogan “Sí, se puede.”

name: Larry Itliong
bio: A Filipino farmworker organizer who led the walkout that began the 1965 Delano grape strike.

name: Harvey Milk
bio: One of the first openly gay elected officials in the US, assassinated in San Francisco City Hall.

name: Marsha P. Johnson
bio: A Black trans activist, a figure of the Stonewall uprising, and co-founder of STAR to shelter trans youth.

name: Sylvia Rivera
bio: A Latina trans activist, Stonewall veteran and co-founder of STAR.

name: Audre Lorde
bio: A Black lesbian poet and essayist who wrote that the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house.

name: Grace Lee Boggs
bio: A Detroit philosopher and activist who worked with C. L. R. James and spent seven decades organizing for community self-reliance.

name: Angela Davis
bio: A philosopher and communist who was acquitted after a high-profile trial and became a leading voice for prison abolition.

name: Paulo Freire
bio: A Brazilian educator who taught peasants to read through their own experience and wrote Pedagogy of the Oppressed.

name: Edward Said
bio: A Palestinian-American literary critic who wrote Orientalism and argued for Palestinian rights.

name: Ghassan Kanafani
bio: A Palestinian novelist and leftist who wrote Men in the Sun. He was killed by a car bomb in Beirut.

name: Mehdi Ben Barka
bio: A Moroccan socialist and organizer of the Tricontinental Conference, abducted in Paris months before it opened and never seen again.

name: Chico Mendes
bio: A Brazilian rubber tapper and union leader who organized to protect the Amazon. He was murdered by a rancher.

name: Ken Saro-Wiwa
bio: A Nigerian writer who led the Ogoni campaign against oil pollution and was hanged by the military government.

name: Berta Cáceres
bio: A Lenca environmental leader in Honduras who was murdered after leading opposition to a dam on a sacred river.

name: Wangari Maathai
bio: A Kenyan biologist who founded the Green Belt Movement, which planted tens of millions of trees, and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Rigoberta Menchú
bio: A K’iche’ Maya activist who exposed the Guatemalan army’s violence against Indigenous people and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Sitting Bull
bio: A Hunkpapa Lakota leader who led resistance to US seizure of the Black Hills and was killed by reservation police.

name: José Rizal
bio: A Filipino writer whose novels exposed Spanish colonial abuses. He was executed in Manila.

name: Andrés Bonifacio
bio: A founder of the Katipunan, which launched the Philippine Revolution against Spain.

name: Qiu Jin
bio: A Chinese feminist and revolutionary who was beheaded after a failed uprising against the Qing dynasty.

name: Kanno Sugako
bio: A Japanese anarchist feminist journalist executed in the High Treason Incident, the only woman among those hanged.

name: Jean Jaurès
bio: A French socialist leader who campaigned to stop the First World War and was assassinated days before it began.

name: Keir Hardie
bio: A Scottish miner and founder of the Labour Party who opposed the First World War.

name: Tommy Douglas
bio: A socialist premier of Saskatchewan who brought in North America’s first single-payer public health insurance.

name: Bobby Sands
bio: An Irish republican prisoner elected to the British Parliament during a hunger strike, on which he died at 27.
